        current = current.next
        root.right = build(mid + 1, hi)
        return root

    return build(0, n - 1)

def reverse_even_length_groups(head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
    prev = head          # the first group has length 1 and is never reversed
    size = 2
    while prev.next:
        # Count the nodes actually present in this group.
        count, after = 0, prev.next
        while after and count < size:
            count += 1
            after = after.next
        if count % 2 == 0:
            first = prev.next
            cur, back = first, after
            for _ in range(count):        # reverse the group in place
                nxt = cur.next
                cur.next = back
                back = cur
                cur = nxt
            prev.next = back              # new front of the group
            prev = first                  # old front is now the tail
        else:
            for _ in range(count):
                prev = prev.next
        size += 1
    return head

Computing that minimum naively costs O(n) per entry. Instead, sweep `i` left to right with a stack of indices whose difficulties are decreasing. Each stack entry `j` stands for all last blocks whose maximum is `jobs[j]`, and `cur[j] - jobs[j]` is the cheapest cost before such a block. When `jobs[i]` is at least `jobs[j]`, those blocks extended to `i` now have maximum `jobs[i]`, so we pop `j` and consider `cur[j] - jobs[j] + jobs[i]`. If the stack is not empty afterwards, its top has a larger maximum that also covers `i`, so `cur[top]` is another candidate. Starting a fresh block at `i` gives `prev[i - 1] + jobs[i]`.
Each index is pushed and popped at most once per day, so each row takes O(n) and the whole run O(n * d). Only two rows are kept.

def min_difficulty(job_difficulty: list[int], d: int) -> int:
    jobs = job_difficulty
    n = len(jobs)
    if n < d:
        return -1
    INF = float("inf")
    # Day 1: the only block is jobs[0..i].
    prev, running = [0] * n, 0
    for i, v in enumerate(jobs):
        running = max(running, v)
        prev[i] = running

    for day in range(2, d + 1):
        cur = [INF] * n
        stack = []   # indices with strictly decreasing job difficulty
        for i in range(day - 1, n):
            best = prev[i - 1] + jobs[i]          # last block is just job i
            while stack and jobs[stack[-1]] <= jobs[i]:
                j = stack.pop()
                # blocks whose max was jobs[j] now have max jobs[i]
                best = min(best, cur[j] - jobs[j] + jobs[i])
            if stack:
                best = min(best, cur[stack[-1]])  # larger max already covers i
            cur[i] = best
            stack.append(i)
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
